description: Single-panel equilibrium phase diagram — the "(b)" panel of a two-panel Figure 1, supplied here without the "(a)" processing-route schematic. The abscissa is Temperature (°C), labelled 500 to 1100 with ticks at 100 °C intervals; the ordinate is Volume fraction (%), labelled 0 to 100 with ticks every 20%. Four labelled curves are plotted: "Austenite" (purple, uppermost), "B2" (red, middle), "κ-carbide" (cyan, lower) and "VC" (yellow, on the baseline). The austenite curve starts at 500 °C just below the 60% level, rises to a broad plateau just under the 80% level between roughly 800 and 950 °C, then declines slightly toward 1100 °C. B2 starts a little above the 20% level at 500 °C, passes through a shallow minimum around 800–900 °C and increases again at 1100 °C. The κ-carbide curve falls from about the 15% level at 500 °C to zero at approximately 780 °C and stays at zero up to 1100 °C. The VC curve lies on the 0% baseline across the whole range, i.e. negligible on this scale. The diagram supports the argument that austenite and B2 coexist with VC precipitation at 900 °C, the condition used for solution treatment.

subfigures.description: Thermo-Calc-style equilibrium phase diagram of the duplex lightweight steel: volume fraction (%) versus temperature (°C, 500–1100). Labelled curves are Austenite (purple, maximum just under 80% at ~800–950 °C), B2 (red, ~20–27%), κ-carbide (cyan, falls to zero near 780 °C) and VC (yellow, at ~0% throughout).

observations.observation: The panel plots Volume fraction (%) on the y-axis (0–100, ticks every 20%) against Temperature (°C) on the x-axis (500–1100, ticks every 100 °C).

The 'Austenite' curve (purple) is the highest in the diagram, rising from just below the 60% level at 500 °C to a plateau just under the 80% level between about 800 and 950 °C, then decreasing slightly toward 1100 °C.
The 'B2' curve (red) lies a little above the 20% level at 500 °C, shows a shallow minimum around 800–900 °C, and rises again toward 1100 °C.
The 'κ-carbide' curve (cyan) decreases from roughly the 15% level at 500 °C and reaches zero at approximately 780 °C, remaining at zero to 1100 °C.
The 'VC' curve (yellow) lies on the 0% baseline across the entire 500–1100 °C range, so its volume fraction is negligible at the scale of this plot.
At 900 °C the diagram shows austenite as the majority phase just below 80%, B2 near the 20% level, and VC at approximately zero.
The caption identifies this panel as the equilibrium phase diagram of the duplex lightweight steel (Figure 1b).
The caption states that Figure 1a is the processing route, which is not included in the supplied image.
The citing text states the phase diagram was calculated with Thermo-Calc 2021b and indicates coexistence of austenite and B2 phases at 900 °C, along with precipitation of VC.
The citing text states the XRD-quantified B2 phase fraction (V_B2) is 20%, consistent with the phase diagram prediction at 900 °C.
The image labels a 'κ-carbide' phase that is not mentioned in either the caption or the citing sentences, which refer only to austenite, B2 and VC; the two accounts differ in the phases named.
A small triangular logo in the lower-left corner of the plot is illegible at the supplied resolution.
